audit.why: Both layers already read Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Maokai / Skill / Gwen / Skill, which is exactly the packet chart and exactly what the mirror audit set on its side. Full and content agree row for row and every why supports its row.
audit.corrected: No chart edits proposed — this is the one matchup in my slice where the chart was already right in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phase whys were boilerplate with no spike and no number, even though the content layer's spikes were already specific.
audit.why: The spike structure here is sharp — Maokai owns 1 through 5 because Gwen has nothing to heal back with, and loses the moment Riftmaker or Nashor's lands — and the full layer said none of it.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten with real numbers: W falling to 11s and Q to 5.5s at 4-5, Skip 'n Slash's 13s with its on-hit refund, R as 3000-range gank setup, and the first-item flip named as Riftmaker/Nashor's.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Hallowed Mist as a wall you have to wait out — 'She's safe inside. Fight when down', 'root her off mist', 'fight her in the mist' listed as a mistake. Riot's text says she 'summons mist that protects her from enemies OUTSIDE of it. She can only be targeted by enemies who ENTER the mist.'
audit.why: The counterplay is inverted. Maokai is a 525-range melee with a point-and-click dash — walking into the mist restores his ability to target her, which is exactly what he wants to do anyway. A player told to wait 22 seconds at the edge gives up the trade for free.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[2].why and breakdown.cooldowns: step into the mist rather than wait at the edge. The mirror audit inverted the same ordering on its side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Skip 'n Slash was described only as an 'E-dash' with no cooldown, and nothing said the cooldown is partially refunded when she hits something.
audit.why: It means the dash is effectively up far more often than 13s in a trade where she is connecting, so 'bait her E-dash then W-root' only works if she whiffs it — a distinction the page never draws.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns and tradeGood.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood and dosFull[1].d refer to Gwen as 'his answer' and 'his every path'.
audit.why: Wrong-pronoun boilerplate on a paying page reads as machine-generated and undercuts the rest.
audit.corrected: tradeGood rewritten in her pronouns and made specific to Skip 'n Slash and the mist edge.

edits.before: Passive heal + AA trades carry the early waves. Identify how Gwen contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: Twisted Advance is point-and-click at 525 and she has no Hallowed Mist yet. Step on her before W exists.

edits.before: W root is your engage AND your peel — spend it once per fight. Only take the trade when Gwen's Hallowed Mist is down.
edits.after: Level 2 gives you W into Q, but Skip 'n Slash refunds its own 13s cooldown on hit, so she can slip the all-in. Coin flip.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gwen must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Hallowed Mist only protects her from enemies outside it. Walk into the mist and she is targetable again — don't wait at the edge.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Hallowed Mist's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your window: W falls to 11s and Q to 5.5s while a pre-item Gwen has nothing to heal back. Repeat the root and grind her out.

edits.before: Nature’s Grasp roots whole teams — lane it only for kill windows. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gwen's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp is 3000-range gank setup, not a duel button — she drops Mist and untargets it. Use 6 to roam, not to force a 1v1.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Hallowed Mist's cooldown.
edits.after: Her item, not yours — Riftmaker or Nashor's turns Snip Snip's true damage on your resistances.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gwen carry threat 9.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on it splits: she wins the 1v1, you win the fight. Lock her down with R for your carries instead of duelling her.

edits.before: - Gwen Hallowed Mist: matchup-defining — She’s safe inside. Fight when down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gwen Hallowed Mist: matchup-defining — 22s at rank 1, and it only stops enemies OUTSIDE it. Step into the mist and she is targetable. - Skip 'n Slash: 13s, but hitting you refunds part of it. - Needlework: 120s, three casts.

edits.before: W-root Gwen the moment his answer is down, Q-knockback the follow-up, and let brush saplings tax his every path.
edits.after: W-root her the moment Skip 'n Slash is spent, Q-knockback the follow-up, and sapling the mist edge she repositions to.

notes: The mist correction and the current wording of dontsFull[1] ('Fight her in the mist' listed as a critical don't) now point in opposite directions. I did not rewrite dontsFull[1].t because a 25-character title swap plus its .d would need to be reasoned about together with report[11], which repeats the same list verbatim; flagging it so a later pass or the user can decide. Also carried over from the mirror: Bramble Smash has derived 'grounding' and 'knockup' flags that Riot's description does not support (knockback and slow only). If Q does in fact ground, it would stop Skip 'n Slash and would be the most important line on this page — worth a human check, and I asserted nothing either way.
